# Demo datasets

Small synthetic datasets, generated by `python tests/seed_data.py`. Everything
here is made up — no real-world or licensed data — so the repo stays tiny and
freely redistributable.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `parcels.geojson` | 25 square parcels in a 5×5 grid near Pune (EPSG:4326). Fields: `id`, `district` (D0/D1/D2), `population` (137 … 3425). |
| `overlay.geojson` | One 3×3-parcel polygon covering the SW corner — the clip/erase mask. |
| `wells.geojson` | 20 points (EPSG:4326) with a `kind` field (well/tank). |
| `landcover.tif` | 240×240 int32 GeoTIFF (EPSG:32643), four class blocks (10/20/30/40) with a `-9999` nodata border. |

## Regenerate them

```bash
python tests/seed_data.py
```

That also loads `parcels`, `overlay` and `wells` into PostGIS as `public.*`
tables, which is what the `-from-table` endpoints read.

## Known-good results

The test suite asserts these exact numbers, so they double as worked examples:

| Operation | Expected |
|---|---|
| buffer 500 m on parcels | 25 features, ~3.4× area |
| buffer `district='D1'` + dissolve | 1 feature |
| split by `district` | 3 outputs (10 / 10 / 5) |
| split grid 2×2 | 4 outputs |
| combine parcels + overlay | 26 features |
| trim by overlay | 9 features (erase → 16; 9 + 16 = 25) |
| vector→raster, `population` @ 30 m | 178×186 px, max 3425 |
| raster→vector on landcover | 4 polygons, classes 10/20/30/40 |
